Through: Mr. Nawal Kishore 
 with Si Baljit S
 Respondent No.2 
 Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Manoj Kumar Ohri
 Order

The present proceedings are instituted under Section 482 Cr.P.C. on behalf of the petitioners seeking quashing of FIR No. 0310/2019 registered under Sections 406/420/34 IPC at P.S. Nabi Karim, Delhi on the ground that the parties have amicably settled their disputes.
2. The allegations in the present FIR relate to fraud by the petitioner on the pretext of getting a job to the complainant in Railways.
3. Mr. Jha, learned APP for the State, on instructions, submits that the petitioners are the only accused persons and respondent No.2 is the complainant/victim in the present case.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners and respondent No. 2 have amicably settled their disputes vide Compromise Deed dated 12.12.2019, a copy of which has been placed on record.
In terms of the said settlement, complainant is now left with no claim or grievance against the petitioners.

sentences.text: 5. Petitioners, who are present in Court, have been identified by the I.O./SI Baljit Singh, Special Staff.
Petitioners have shown remorse for their conduct and undertake not to repeat the same in future.
6. Respondent No. 2, who is in person alongwith his counsel, has been identified by the I.O.
He states that he has settled the disputes with the petitioners out of his own free will, volition and without any coercion.
He states that he has no objection if the present FIR and consequent proceedings are quashed.
7. The parties shall remain bound by the statements made in Court today.

8. In Parbatbhai Aahir and Others v. State of Gujarat and Another reported as (2017) 9 SCC 641, it has been held as under:-

sentences.text:
The broad principles which emerge from the precedents on the subject, may be summarised in the following propositions:
xxx 16.7.
As distinguished from serious offences, there may be criminal cases which have an overwhelming or predominant element of a civil dispute.

They stand on a distinct footing in so far as the exercise of the inherent power to quash is concerned;
16.8.

In such a case, the High Court may quash the criminal proceeding if in view of the compromise between the disputants, the possibility of a conviction is remote and the continuation of a criminal proceeding would cause oppression and prejudice;
and..."

Considering the law on the point and the other decisions of this Court on the point, referred to hereinabove, it is observed and held as under:
15.1.

That the power conferred Under Section 482 of the Code to quash the criminal proceedings for the non-compoundable offences Under Section 320 of the Code can be exercised having overwhelmingly and predominantly the civil character,

sentences.text: In view of the above facts and considering that no useful purpose will be served in continuance of the proceedings, it is directed that the aforesaid FIR and the consequent proceedings arising therefrom are hereby quashed, subject to payment of cost of Rs.25,000/- to be paid by each of the petitioners to the respondent No.2 through demand draft(s) through the I.O. within four weeks from today.

11. Proof evidencing receipt of deposit shall be filed with the I.O. as well as in Court failing which,
the Registry shall list the matter in the Court.
12. A copy of this order be communicated to the Member Secretary, Delhi State Legal Services Authority for intimation.
13. With the above directions, the petition is disposed of.
